statement: On the 8-pin NE555 (KiCad Timer:NE555D), RESET is pin 4 (active-low). If RESET is unused, short it to VCC (pin 8); if it is used, pull it up to VCC. CONT is pin 5; decoupling it to ground with 0.01 µF can improve astable operation.
condition: Any NE555 / NA555 / SA555 / SE555 in D, P, PS, or PW packages.

values.RESET: pin 4, tie to VCC if unused

statement: NE555 astable (Figure 6-5): RA from VCC to DISCH (pin 7), RB from DISCH to THRES (pin 6) tied to TRIG (pin 2), C from that node to GND. tH ≈ 0.693·(RA+RB)·C, tL ≈ 0.693·RB·C, f ≈ 1.44/((RA+2RB)·C). Decouple CONT (pin 5) with 0.01 µF to GND.
condition: Standard 555 astable using the 8-pin SOIC/PDIP pinout.

statement: LM386 voltage gain is 20 (26 dB) with pins 1 and 8 open. A capacitor from pin 1 to pin 8 raises gain to 200 (46 dB); 10 µF is the typical-application value. The minimum-parts output network is 0.05 µF in series with 10 Ω from VOUT (pin 5) to GND, plus a 250 µF coupling capacitor to the speaker. Bypass (pin 7) may take 10 µF to GND.

statement: AMS1117 requires an output capacitor as frequency compensation; 22 µF solid tantalum on the output covers all operating conditions, including when the ADJ pin is bypassed. Dropout (VIN−VOUT) is typically 1.1 V and guaranteed 1.3 V max at 0.8 A. SOT-223 pins: 1 = GND/ADJ, 2 = VOUT, 3 = VIN.
condition: AMS1117 adjustable or fixed linear regulator.

statement: MCP6001 VDD (1.8 V to 6.0 V) needs a local bypass of 0.01 µF to 0.1 µF within 2 mm of the supply pin, plus a bulk capacitor of 1 µF or larger within 100 mm (that bulk cap may be shared with nearby analog parts). An unused amplifier in a dual/quad package must not float: buffer a mid-supply divider or tie the unused op amp as in Figure 4-5.
condition: MCP6001/2/4 family op amp on a single positive supply.

statement: TMP100 SCL (pin 1) and SDA (pin 6) are open-drain and each require a pull-up resistor; 5 kΩ is the recommended value and the pin current must stay ≤ 3 mA. V+ (pin 4) is 2.7 V to 5.5 V. Figure 12 shows a 0.01 µF supply bypass at V+; §8.2.1 also lists 0.1 µF as a recommended bypass. Place the bypass as close as possible to V+ and GND (pin 2).
condition: TMP100 (or TMP101) on an I2C/SMBus with a two-wire host.

statement: TMP100 ADD0 (pin 5) and ADD1 (pin 3) each connect to GND, V+, or float, giving eight I2C slave addresses (Table 2). ADD1=0 ADD0=0 → 1001000. The pin state is sampled on the first bus communication and must be set before any I2C activity; after that it is latched.
condition: TMP100 on a shared I2C bus; one or more devices.

statement: STM32G474 each VDD/VSS pair is decoupled with n×100 nF plus one 4.7 µF; VDDA/VSSA uses 10 nF plus 1 µF; VREF+ uses 100 nF plus 1 µF. Place the ceramics as close as possible to, or under, the pins. KiCad MCU_ST_STM32G4:STM32G474RETx.
condition: STM32G474xB/xC/xE minimum power scheme, including STM32G474RET6.

statement: A Pierce crystal on OSC_IN/OSC_OUT sees CL = (CL1·CL2)/(CL1+CL2) + Cs. CL is the crystal's specified load; Cs is MCU pin plus PCB stray. With CL1 = CL2, each external capacitor is 2·(CL − Cs). Example in the note: CL = 15 pF and Cs = 5 pF → CL1 = CL2 = 20 pF.
condition: HSE or LSE Pierce oscillator on an STM32/STM8 with two external load capacitors.
formula: CL = (CL1 * CL2) / (CL1 + CL2) + Cs; CL1 = CL2 = 2 * (CL - Cs)
